title: Analytica explicatio methodi maximorum et minimorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E297 recasts the calculus of variations in Lagrange's δ-algorithm. This page finishes the solution of Problem 4. The problem is to make J = ∫_0^a Z dx extremal, where Z depends on x, y, p = y', q = y'', r, … and on a running integral Φ(x) = ∫_0^x 𝔷 dx. Here 𝔷 itself depends on x, y, p, q, … and on a second running integral φ = ∫𝔷 dx, whose integrand depends only on x, y, p, q, ….

The partial derivatives are named as follows:
- for Z: ∂Z/∂Φ = L, and N, P, Q, R for y, p, q, r;
- for the middle integrand: 𝔏, 𝔑, 𝔓, 𝔔, 𝔑;
- for the innermost integrand: 𝔫, 𝔭, 𝔮, 𝔯.

State of play from the previous page. With w = 𝔫δy + 𝔭δp + 𝔮δq + … and v = ∫𝔏 dx, Euler had integrated by parts to get
δΦ = v∫w dx + ∫dx[δy(𝔑 − v𝔫) + δp(𝔓 − v𝔭) + …].

On this page:
1. Put V = ∫L dx and T = ∫Lv dx.
2. Integrate by parts once more:
 ∫L δΦ dx = T∫w dx − ∫T w dx + V∫(…)dx − ∫V(…)dx.
3. Collect the coefficient of δy under the integral:
 N − V(𝔑 − v𝔫) − T𝔫 = N − V𝔑 + (Vv − T)𝔫.
 The same pattern holds for P, Q, R.
4. The boundary products at x = a (T(a)∫_0^a w, V(a)∫_0^a(…)) are removed by choosing the integration constants so that V(a) = T(a) = 0.
5. Define (N) = N − V𝔑 + (Vv − T)𝔫, and similarly (P), (Q), (R). The variation then has exactly the form of the simplest case:
 δJ = ∫dx δy[(N) − d(P)/dx + d²(Q)/dx² − …] + boundary terms δy[(P) − d(Q)/dx + …] + (dδy/dx)[(Q) − …] + …
 The Euler–Lagrange equation is (N) − d(P)/dx + … = 0.

Corollary 1. Since d(Vv) = Lv dx + 𝔏V dx, we have Vv − T = ∫𝔏V dx =: 𝔙. It also vanishes at x = a. So the auxiliary variable v, whose additive constant is irrelevant, can be eliminated.

Corollary 2. The result reduces to two auxiliary functions:
- V with V' = L, V(a) = 0;
- 𝔙 with 𝔙' = 𝔏V, 𝔙(a) = 0.
Then (N) = N − V𝔑 + 𝔙𝔫, and so on.

In modern terms, V and 𝔙 are (up to sign) the costates/Lagrange multipliers of the state equations Φ' = 𝔷 and φ' = 𝔷. They satisfy a backward chain of adjoint ODEs with zero terminal values, i.e. transversality at the free end x = a.

The next page generalises to arbitrary nesting depth (Coroll. 3). Problem 5 then treats the self-referential case Φ' = 𝔷(x, y, Φ, …) via an integrating factor e^{∫𝔏 dx}, which is the linear adjoint equation.
errors: No mathematical errors found. The integrations by parts, the collected coefficients N − V𝔑 + (Vv − T)𝔫, and the identity Vv − T = ∫𝔏V dx are all correct.

Minor point: the boundary terms at x = 0 are left implicit. The 'etc.' boundary expressions are to be read as differences of values at a and 0, as in the earlier problems. This is consistent with Euler's convention but not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Variation of a functional whose integrand depends on nested running integrals (integral of an integral), reduced to an ordinary Euler–Lagrange equation with modified coefficients (N), (P), …
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange equations for integro-differential (non-local, nested) Lagrangians; equivalently, Lagrange-multiplier treatment of auxiliary state equations Φ' = 𝔷, φ' = 𝔷
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Ch. III (formulae involving indefinite integrals); recast here in Lagrange's δ-calculus
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (E65, 1744), Ch. III; E297 itself (Novi Comm. 10, 1766)

ideas.what: Auxiliary functions V = ∫L dx and 𝔙 = ∫𝔏V dx with integration constants chosen to vanish at the upper end x = a, so that boundary terms drop out
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint/costate variables solved backward with terminal condition zero (transversality at a free end); chain of adjoint equations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744) in substance; adjoint/costate formalism attributed to Lagrange multipliers and later Pontryagin et al. (1956–62) in optimal control
ideas.where_published: E65 Ch. III (Euler's quantity V there plays the same role); E297

ideas.what: Elimination of the intermediate v via integration by parts: Vv − T = ∫𝔏V dx
ideas.modern_name: Integration by parts / Fubini interchange for iterated integrals (∫_x^a of nested kernels)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful δ-calculus rederivation of results Euler had already obtained in Methodus inveniendi Ch. III. The costate-like structure (backward integrals vanishing at the end point) is striking from an optimal-control viewpoint. However, the link between Euler's Ch. III 'V' quantities and adjoint variables is noted in historical studies of the calculus of variations, so nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: In the image the subtracted terms read '-∫T dx(𝔫δy + 𝔭δp + 𝔮δq + 𝔯δr + etc.)' and '-∫V dx δy(𝔑-v𝔫) …', as transcribed.
Coroll. 1 reads 'Vv-T = ∫L dx·∫𝔏 dx - ∫L dx∫𝔏 dx = ∫𝔏 dx∫L dx': the last expression means ∫(𝔏·∫L dx)dx, i.e. ∫𝔏V dx.
